pros.title: Strengths will show once braking assist is off
pros.detail: With the assist braking for you, the data mostly shows what the assist did.

cons.title: Braking assist was on
cons.detail: The game braked for you (your brake pedal was idle while the car braked hard), so braking and throttle technique can't be judged from this session. Lap times and consistency below still count.

cons.title: Busy hands: steering corrections mid-corner (T2, T3, T5)
cons.detail: Repeated small corrections mean the car is moving around under you or the line needs adjusting mid-corner. Both cost speed.

cons.title: Not using all the road on exit (T1, T3, T5)
cons.detail: T1: about 3.7 m more was available; T3: about 3 m more was available; T5: about 5 m more was available. Using the full width lets you straighten the wheel and get on the throttle sooner.

cons.title: Inconsistent through T5, T3, T2, T4, T1
cons.detail: T5: 0.66 s between your average and best pass; T3: 0.56 s between your average and best pass; T2: 0.55 s between your average and best pass; T4: 0.35 s between your average and best pass; T1: 0.32 s between your average and best pass.

improve.title: Turn braking assist off
improve.target: Your own braking in the data
improve.how: Start with braking assist off in a slow, forgiving car (like this Caterham) and brake early. Expect slower laps at first; that is normal while you learn your own brake points.

improve.title: Use all the road on exit
improve.target: Let the car run out to the edge on every exit
improve.how: In T1, T3, T5, aim to finish the corner right at the outside edge. If you're not getting there, you're probably apexing too late or lifting; commit to the throttle and let the car drift out.

improve.title: Pick fixed reference points
improve.how: For T5, T3, T2: choose one brake marker (a board, a shadow, a kerb start) and one turn-in point, and use them every lap. Move the brake marker 5 m later only when you hit the apex 3 laps in a row.

stopDoing.title: Relying on braking assist
stopDoing.detail: It brakes conservatively and stops you learning brake points, trail braking and how the car feels at the limit.

stopDoing.title: Sawing at the wheel
stopDoing.detail: One smooth turn in, hold, one smooth unwind. If you need to correct, the input before it was too sudden or too early.

show.why: The single most useful number. It turns green/red within a corner, so you instantly know whether a change you just tried worked.
Shows trail braking and throttle overlap at a glance. Optional once your technique is consistent.
Your ES wheel already has RPM LEDs, so you don't need to look at the HUD for shifts. Keep the gear number visible.

pros.title: You commit to the brake pedal in 4 of 5 braking zones
pros.detail: You hit 90-100% brake pressure in T1, T2, T3, T4. Many newer drivers never press hard enough; you do, and that's the foundation of late braking.

pros.title: Fast, decisive brake application (T1, T2, T3, T4, T5)
pros.detail: You reach peak pressure in under 0.2 s. That is exactly right: the first part of the braking zone is where the tyres have the most grip.

pros.title: You get back on the throttle at the slowest point in 5 corners
pros.detail: Picking up the throttle at the apex (not after it) is good timing. The problem is what happens just before that point; see weaknesses.

pros.title: Very few locked wheels
pros.detail: You are not flat-spotting tyres under braking.

cons.title: Coasting: 27.4% of the lap with neither pedal pressed
cons.detail: About 181 m per lap in T2, T3, T4, T5. You come off the brake, roll, and only then pick up the throttle. The car is slowing with nothing controlling its balance, so you lose time and the front goes light before the apex.

cons.title: Braking into ABS in 2 corners
cons.detail: In T1, T5 ABS is active for 57% of the zone at worst. ABS is a safety net; leaning on it lengthens your stops and hides where the real limit is.

cons.title: Rear wheelspin on exit in 5 corners
cons.detail: T1, T2, T3, T4, T5. Spinning wheels don't accelerate the car; they just cook the tyres.

cons.title: Busy hands: steering corrections mid-corner (T1, T2, T5)
cons.detail: Repeated small corrections mean the car is moving around under you or the line needs adjusting mid-corner. Both cost speed.

cons.title: Inconsistent through T2
cons.detail: T2: 0.83 s between your average and best pass.

improve.title: Connect the brake to the throttle
improve.target: Coasting under 8% of the lap, and under 10 m in any corner
improve.how: Keep 10-20% brake on as you turn in and hold it until the slowest point, then go straight to a light throttle. No gap between the pedals. Practice only this for 5 laps, starting with T3, T5.

improve.title: Threshold braking: hard first, then bleed off
improve.target: ABS active less than 20% of each braking zone
improve.how: Hit the brake hard first, and the moment ABS starts working, ease off 5-10% instead of holding the pedal down.

improve.title: Squeeze the throttle on exits
improve.target: Rear tyres within ~10°C of the fronts; no wheelspin flags
improve.how: In slow corners take about a second to go from 0 to 100% throttle, and only go to full once the steering is unwinding. Short-shift (change up early) out of hairpins. Consider turning traction control on while you learn.

improve.title: Pick fixed reference points
improve.how: For T2: choose one brake marker (a board, a shadow, a kerb start) and one turn-in point, and use them every lap. Move the brake marker 5 m later only when you hit the apex 3 laps in a row.

stopDoing.title: Letting go of both pedals between braking and the apex
stopDoing.detail: Every metre without a pedal is time you are not using.

stopDoing.title: Holding the brake pedal flat and letting ABS do the work
stopDoing.detail: Ease off as soon as you feel ABS chatter or see the ABS light.

stopDoing.title: Going to full throttle while the car is still turning
stopDoing.detail: Add throttle as you take steering lock off, not before.

stopDoing.title: Sawing at the wheel
stopDoing.detail: One smooth turn in, hold, one smooth unwind. If you need to correct, the input before it was too sudden or too early.

setup.title: No consistent balance problem detected
setup.detail: Handling looks reasonably neutral from the data. Focus on driving technique first.

setup.title: FL: inside only 1.4°C hotter than outside
setup.detail: Not enough negative camber; the outside edge is working too hard. Add about 0.2-0.3° negative camber.

setup.title: RL: inside only -0.8°C hotter than outside
setup.detail: Not enough negative camber; the outside edge is working too hard. Add about 0.2-0.3° negative camber.

pros.title: You commit to the brake pedal in 3 of 4 braking zones
pros.detail: You hit 90-100% brake pressure in T1, T2, T3. Many newer drivers never press hard enough; you do, and that's the foundation of late braking.

pros.title: Fast, decisive brake application (T1, T3)
pros.detail: You reach peak pressure in under 0.2 s. That is exactly right: the first part of the braking zone is where the tyres have the most grip.

pros.title: You get back on the throttle at the slowest point in 4 corners
pros.detail: Picking up the throttle at the apex (not after it) is good timing. The problem is what happens just before that point; see weaknesses.

pros.title: Very few locked wheels
pros.detail: You are not flat-spotting tyres under braking.

cons.title: Coasting: 29.4% of the lap with neither pedal pressed
cons.detail: About 157 m per lap in T1, T2, T3, T4. You come off the brake, roll, and only then pick up the throttle. The car is slowing with nothing controlling its balance, so you lose time and the front goes light before the apex.

cons.title: Braking into ABS in 1 corners
cons.detail: In T1 ABS is active for 38% of the zone at worst. ABS is a safety net; leaning on it lengthens your stops and hides where the real limit is.

cons.title: Rear wheelspin on exit in 4 corners
cons.detail: T1, T2, T3, T4. Spinning wheels don't accelerate the car; they just cook the tyres.

cons.title: Slow to build brake pressure (T2, T4)
cons.detail: It takes you 0.74 s / 0.36 s to reach peak. Aim for 0.1-0.2 s.

cons.title: Running wide of the apex (T1)
cons.detail: T1: 1.6 m wider than your best lap. Missing the apex makes the corner longer and slower.

cons.title: Busy hands: steering corrections mid-corner (T1, T2, T3)
cons.detail: Repeated small corrections mean the car is moving around under you or the line needs adjusting mid-corner. Both cost speed.

cons.title: Inconsistent through T2
cons.detail: T2: 0.16 s between your average and best pass.

improve.title: Connect the brake to the throttle
improve.target: Coasting under 8% of the lap, and under 10 m in any corner
improve.how: Keep 10-20% brake on as you turn in and hold it until the slowest point, then go straight to a light throttle. No gap between the pedals. Practice only this for 5 laps, starting with T3, T4.

improve.title: Threshold braking: hard first, then bleed off
improve.target: ABS active less than 20% of each braking zone
improve.how: Hit the brake hard first, and the moment ABS starts working, ease off 5-10% instead of holding the pedal down.

improve.title: Squeeze the throttle on exits
improve.target: Rear tyres within ~10°C of the fronts; no wheelspin flags
improve.how: In slow corners take about a second to go from 0 to 100% throttle, and only go to full once the steering is unwinding. Short-shift (change up early) out of hairpins. Consider turning traction control on while you learn.

improve.title: Hit the apex
improve.target: Within 0.5 m of your best line at every apex
improve.how: In T1, turn in slightly later and aim the car at the inside kerb. If you still can't reach it, you're carrying too much speed in: brake a touch more.

stopDoing.title: Letting go of both pedals between braking and the apex
stopDoing.detail: Every metre without a pedal is time you are not using.

stopDoing.title: Holding the brake pedal flat and letting ABS do the work
stopDoing.detail: Ease off as soon as you feel ABS chatter or see the ABS light.

stopDoing.title: Going to full throttle while the car is still turning
stopDoing.detail: Add throttle as you take steering lock off, not before.

stopDoing.title: Sawing at the wheel
stopDoing.detail: One smooth turn in, hold, one smooth unwind. If you need to correct, the input before it was too sudden or too early.

show.item: Live delta to your best lap
show.why: The single most useful number. It turns green/red within a corner, so you instantly know whether a change you just tried worked.
Keep these on while you fix coasting (29.4% now): you'll see the gap between the red and green bars. Remove once it's under 8%.
Your ES wheel already has RPM LEDs, so you don't need to look at the HUD for shifts. Keep the gear number visible.

show.item: Last lap and best lap times
show.why: Glance on the main straight only.
Check after a few laps to see if you are overheating one end.

hide.item: Full standings / timing tower in practice
hide.why: Irrelevant when you are learning. Use the relative (gap to cars around you) only in races.
Useful for your first laps on a new track. After that, learn the track by real reference points instead.
Never read numbers in a corner. Look through the corner to the apex and exit; read the HUD only on straights.
Only matter in long races. Hide them in practice to reduce clutter.

settings: Let AMS2 set steering lock for each car, and watch the FFB meter for clipping.

traits.name: Speed
traits.text: Quick. Braking points come up fast.

traits.name: Cornering grip
traits.text: Low grip: the car slides early, so be smooth and patient.

traits.name: Wheelspin tendency
traits.text: Spins the wheels easily: squeeze the throttle on gradually out of every corner.

traits.name: Downforce
traits.text: No downforce: grip is the same at any speed.

traits.name: How forgiving
traits.text: Some mistakes will catch you out.

tips: Squeeze the throttle on over about a second out of slow corners; go to full throttle only as you straighten the wheel.
Low grip: brake in a straight line, turn smoothly, and avoid sudden inputs.
